summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the strongest and most robust convergent evidence. It leads the overall convergence ranking and stays in the top ten under most random re-weightings [gene=CA9; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:convergence:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=convergence; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.894]. The protein is clearly raised in tumour compared with normal kidney [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.2686], and the rise is large in TCGA [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.712]. Both single-cell datasets place it in the cancer cells [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.981]. Girentuximab has reached phase 3. CA9 is best read as an antigen for antibodies, imaging and conjugates and as a tissue biomarker, not as a functional dependency: no ccRCC cell line depends on it, and expression is patchy in some donors [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3%].

A second tier of tumour-up candidates follows, and each has a specific weakness. NNMT is made by tumour cells in both single-cell datasets, and its protein rise replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]. Higher expression goes with shorter survival in TCGA [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301], but NNMT has no clinical drug. CD70 has clinical antibodies and the second-best conjugate score [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], but immune cells contribute a large share of its transcripts [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]. SCARB1 tops the target profile [gene=SCARB1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.968] and its protein replicates. Its cell of origin does not replicate, though: myeloid cells dominate in one single-cell dataset [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336]. ENPP3 has a clinical-stage conjugate (AGS-16C3F) but strong kidney and duodenum staining. EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha, belzutifan) remains the only clinically validated axis and the only candidate with a selective, though nominal, ccRCC dependency [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3].

The strongest biomarker calls are genes lost in the tumour, which mark the loss of normal proximal-tubule metabolism. PSAT1 is the most robust biomarker in the analysis [gene=PSAT1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.986], and its protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]. The same holds for PCK1 [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819], whose phosphosites also replicate. These are tissue-state biomarkers, not drug targets, and most of the top of the overall convergence ranking (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1, NPHS2, PIGR) is the same tubule-loss signal. Replication also removes candidates: the HK2 protein rise seen in discovery does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074].

Unexplored candidates. The convergence ranking rewards literature and existing drugs, so it cannot put a little-studied gene on top; those genes come from the separate discovery screen. Here 'novel' means few ccRCC papers (at most fifteen) and no clinical drug, not that nothing has been published. The two best candidates belong to the tumour-cell track, and both are identified and prioritised for experimental validation. COL23A1 is a transmembrane collagen made mainly by the cancer cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. Its protein is higher in tumours [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; protein_log2fc=2.512], the rise replicates in TCGA, and it survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. It also has antibody tractability and little vital-organ RNA. However, only a minority of tumour cells express it [gene=COL23A1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.pct_expressing=17.1%]. RAB42, a small GTPase, is also mainly tumour-cell derived [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627] and holds at full purity [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189], but as an intracellular protein it is doubtful for antibodies. For both genes several things are missing: protein staining in normal tissues, proof of an accessible surface epitope, a selective dependency (neither has one), confirmatory-cohort protein data and a measure of heterogeneity across tumour cells. Immunohistochemistry on tumour and normal tissue microarrays, followed by knockdown and antibody-binding studies in ccRCC models, would test them. The leading immune-track gene, GAL3ST4, is a macrophage gene whose bulk rise largely disappears at full purity [gene=GAL3ST4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401], so it is a microenvironment hypothesis. The literature agent reported no earlier preclinical ccRCC work on these genes in the corpus. Nothing here shows that treating any of them would help a patient.

omics.text: At the protein level, the tumour-up candidates are CA9 [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.2686], CD70 [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.4207], NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709], SLC16A3 (MCT4) [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.2792], SCARB1 [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.8371] and ENPP3 [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.5438]. CA9 also replicates strongly in TCGA RNA. SLC16A3 belongs to the glycolytic, HIF-driven programme of ccRCC, which follows from VHL loss, and it reads better as mechanism than as a selective target.

The strongest losses are metabolic enzymes of the normal tubule: PSAT1 [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.9635], PCK1 [gene=PCK1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.8592] and ALDH6A1, which sits on frequently lost 14q. They separate tumour from normal tissue well, which makes them biomarkers, but losing a normal-tissue enzyme gives nothing to inhibit. VHL [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.4834] and PBRM1 [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362] are the recurrent drivers that explain the HIF-driven programme. They are mechanism and stratification genes, not direct targets.

literature.text: The literature supports CA9, CD70 and NNMT most directly, all at proof-of-concept or preclinical level. For CA9 it reports tumour-cell enrichment with low normal-kidney background and proof-of-concept CA9 PET imaging. For CD70 it reports overexpression with minimal normal-tissue expression and CD70-specific radiotracer antibodies. For NNMT it reports upregulation linked to worse survival, together with selective NNMT inhibitor chemistry that was not tested in ccRCC. ENO2 and COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) have dense mechanistic literature on glycolysis and ferroptosis, but all of it is preclinical. ALDOB, UMOD and PLIN2 have biomarker-only support.

The literature corpus has no extracted relations for several data-strong candidates, including SCARB1, ENPP3, VHL and EPAS1, so the corpus neither supports nor contradicts them. Three directional conflicts are flagged. MT1G is lower in tumours, yet high expression within tumours is adverse. PFKP is tumour-up, yet low expression was linked to poor survival. ABAT is tumour-suppressive, yet has an approved inhibitor. FCER1G and TYROBP are reported as poor-prognosis biomarkers, but their signal looks immune-derived. Most claims rest on one or two bioinformatic papers.

external.text: Open Targets and DepMap split the candidates into two groups. Surface antigens with clinical-stage biologics (CA9 with girentuximab, CD70 with cusatuzumab, ENPP3 with the conjugate AGS-16C3F) show no ccRCC cell-line dependency, so any benefit would come from antibody, imaging or conjugate delivery rather than loss of function. EPAS1 has the approved drug belzutifan and is the only candidate where ccRCC lines are more dependent than other lines, with a minority of lines dependent [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0.208]. Even so, the dependency is borderline after correction [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; padj=0.0609]. SCARB1, SLC16A3, NNMT and ALDOB have no returned drugs, so their target case rests on predicted tractability only.

cells.text: Single-cell attribution separates tumour-intrinsic candidates from microenvironment genes. CA9 [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976] and MET [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935] are carried by the cancer cells. KDR is endothelial [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], and CD74 and CXCR4 are immune-cell genes. Most endothelial cells express EPAS1 [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=81.3%], so a bulk EPAS1 signal mixes tumour and stromal sources. KDR, CD74 and CXCR4 are therefore not tumour-intrinsic, even where bulk omics ranks them. CD70 is mixed: RCC cells have the highest per-cell level, but regulatory and CD8 T cells also express it.

A second single-cell dataset confirms the cell of origin for CA9 [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.981] and NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.948]. It does not confirm SCARB1, whose dominant source switches from myeloid cells to tumour cells between datasets [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582]. PSAT1 is also unresolved [gene=PSAT1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.072]. The tumour-cell attribution of SCARB1, which leads the target profile, therefore remains open.

spatial.text: In Visium sections the composition-corrected in-situ source of CA9 is the tumour cells. High-CA9 spots sit among other tumour spots more often than expected by chance [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381], with only a small macrophage enrichment. The spatial estimates depend on deconvolution, and they support the single-cell attributions rather than adding new candidates.

structure.text: Structural context comes from cavities detected computationally in predicted AlphaFold monomers. It is a descriptive heuristic only and is not evidence of a degron, of ligase compatibility or of degradability. No curated experimental degron or ternary-complex reference was used for these candidates. The CA9 model has a moderate top cavity [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.546], and the detected cavities cover part of its known experimental ligand contacts [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. The COL23A1 model is low confidence [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91] with only a tiny cavity [gene=COL23A1; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.2342], so an antibody against an extracellular domain is the more plausible modality.

discovery.text: COL23A1 is a transmembrane collagen and the leading tumour-track candidate. The cancer cells make most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. It is strongly raised in TCGA tumours [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.8291], and the rise survives extrapolation to a pure tumour, so it is not infiltration [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. It carries no adverse prognosis signal, and it has antibody and protein tractability with low vital-organ RNA. Expression within the tumour is heterogeneous, since only a minority of RCC cells express it [gene=COL23A1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.pct_expressing=17.1%]. A selective dependency, normal-tissue protein staining and confirmatory-cohort protein data are still missing, so it remains a data-ranked hypothesis.

RAB42 is a small Rab GTPase and the second tumour-track candidate. Cancer cells carry most of its transcripts [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]. It is raised in TCGA [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.371] and holds at full purity [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189], with no prognostic signal. Its surface annotation is doubtful for an intracellular GTPase, so antibody access needs checking, and there is no dependency or functional evidence.

The stroma and immune tracks give microenvironment hypotheses, not tumour-cell targets. OLFML2A is a fibroblast gene [gene=OLFML2A; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Fibroblast; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.647] that holds at full purity [gene=OLFML2A; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.527], but it has colon expression. JAG2 is partly endothelial, with a modest effect and expression in heart muscle. GAL3ST4 is a macrophage gene [gene=GAL3ST4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.972] whose bulk rise shrinks at full purity [gene=GAL3ST4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401]. LILRB4 is flagged infiltration-driven, with its signal largely vanishing at full purity [gene=LILRB4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.508]. None of the discovery candidates is a selective dependency.

validation.text: The independent layers strengthen CA9, NNMT and CD70. CA9 stays strongly tumour-up when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=CA9; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=7.787]. CD70 also survives the purity check after a concordant rise in TCGA. NNMT has a prognostic association with shorter survival and replicates at protein level in the confirmatory cohort [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.07e-46]. SCARB1 protein also replicates [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334], but its cell of origin does not. CA9 and CD70 could not be tested in the confirmatory cohort because too few matched pairs exist; this is not a failure to replicate.

The same layers weaken other candidates. HK2 is the clearest case: its discovery protein rise [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_discovery_log2fc=2.106] does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort. None of the tumour-up candidates (CA9, CD70, ENPP3, SCARB1, NNMT) is a ccRCC cell-line dependency. VHL is the dominant somatic driver, mutated in nearly half of patients [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; mutated_patients=247], but it is a tumour suppressor rather than a target. The PSAT1 protein loss replicates, but its single phosphosite does not [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); phosphosites_replicating=0].

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the evidence streams, a small set of calls is stable. In the target profile, SCARB1 [gene=SCARB1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=8], CA9 [gene=CA9; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.941], SLC16A3 [gene=SLC16A3; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.881], CD70, NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.88] and ENPP3 [gene=ENPP3; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.823] stay near the top. In the biomarker profile, PSAT1 [gene=PSAT1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=4] and PCK1 [gene=PCK1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.889] are the robust calls.

Other positions depend on the chosen weights. ALDH6A1 can reach the top of the biomarker profile but has a wide interval [gene=ALDH6A1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=33]. ALDOB, second in the overall convergence ranking, often falls outside the biomarker top twenty-five once the weights vary [gene=ALDOB; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top25=0.486]. In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 is a robust top-ten call [gene=CA9; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:convergence:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=convergence; rank_interval_90.p_top25=0.983], so the overall score should not be read as a fixed ordering.

treatment.text: In IMmotion150, no reviewed candidate shows a significant association with outcome, and no gene separates the two main arms after correction. Higher CD70 points towards longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.383], but the adjusted p-value is not significant [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.166]. CA9 shows a weaker association in the same direction, and its difference between arms is null [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.779]. PSAT1, NNMT and EPAS1 have only small or single-arm results [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab.padj=0.829]. These are association leads, not predictive biomarkers.

subtypes.text: CA9 is the only reviewed candidate flagged as a subgroup candidate, for PBRM1-mutant tumours. The flag is driven by RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971], while the protein difference does not reach significance [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_protein.padj=0.067]. PSAT1 and PCK1 are not subgroup candidates for VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2. PCK1 has a strong ccA/ccB difference in TCGA RNA [gene=PCK1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-2.581] that is absent at protein level. EPAS1 is one of the genes that define the ccA/ccB split. Mutation-group comparisons rest on few mutant cases, and immune genes can differ between groups only through infiltration, so these are hypotheses for stratified studies.

adc.text: For an antibody-drug conjugate or radioligand, CD70 scores highest [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], but there are no normal-tissue staining data, so its safety cannot be judged. CA9 is a good known control [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647], with stomach staining and patchy expression in some donors. ENPP3, another control, stains strongly in kidney and duodenum [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3]. SCARB1 is expressed in very few tumour cells in the weakest donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%] and stains the adrenal gland, which argues against a conjugate. A high suitability score does not show that a conjugate would work.

immune.text: Immune deconvolution separates infiltration genes from tumour-cell genes. FCGR3A is almost entirely immune-derived [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] and tracks the overall immune score, so it marks hot, infiltrated tumours and serves as a control. CD70 sits in between [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]: it correlates with CD8 T-cell content [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_cd8_t_cells=0.278], so part of its signal would weaken in cold tumours. CA9 and NNMT are tumour-cell genes in both single-cell datasets, so their signal should hold in cold tumours too. The immune-track discovery genes (GAL3ST4, LILRB4) and the literature genes FCER1G and TYROBP belong to the infiltration class.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most clearly on CA9: tumour-cell protein increase, literature on imaging and targeting, and clinical-stage antibodies. They also converge on CD70 and NNMT, each with one caveat (immune expression for CD70, no drug for NNMT). The layers disagree on SCARB1 and ENPP3, which are strong in omics but absent from the literature corpus, and on EPAS1, which is weak in bulk tumour-cell expression but is the only validated drug target and the only selective dependency. The top of the overall convergence ranking is dominated by tubule-loss biomarkers (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD), which help classify tissue but are not targets. In short, CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 are antigen-delivery targets, NNMT is a combined target and biomarker hypothesis, and EPAS1 is the mechanism-validated reference. PSAT1 and PCK1 are biomarkers, and SLC16A3, VHL and PBRM1 describe mechanism.

targets.rationale: Most robust convergent call: first overall and second in the target profile [gene=CA9; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.941]. It is a tumour-cell-intrinsic surface antigen with replicated single-cell attribution and clinical-stage antibodies. It has no dependency, and patchy expression limits conjugates.

Surface antigen with clinical antibodies and the second-best conjugate suitability [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746]. It is robust in the target profile and survives the purity check, but it has a substantial immune-cell component and no normal-tissue staining data.

Tumour-cell enzyme whose protein rise replicates in the confirmatory cohort and whose cell of origin replicates in a second single-cell dataset. It has an adverse survival association [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301], but no clinical drug and no cell-line dependency, so the target call is a hypothesis.

Placed above its numeric rank because it is the only clinically validated axis (belzutifan) and the only selective ccRCC dependency [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], although that dependency is borderline after correction. Its transcripts are also abundant in endothelial cells.

Robust in the target profile [gene=ENPP3; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.823], with a clinical-stage conjugate. Strong kidney and duodenum staining and the absence of ccRCC literature in the corpus limit it.

First in the target profile and the most robust there [gene=SCARB1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.968], with replicated protein. Placed below CA9, CD70, NNMT and ENPP3 for four reasons: its tumour-cell attribution does not replicate across single-cell datasets, it is expressed in few tumour cells in some donors, it stains the adrenal gland, and it has no drug or dependency.

MCT4 lactate exporter, robust in the target profile [gene=SLC16A3; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.881] with tumour-up protein. It is better read as part of the glycolytic mechanism, and it has no drug and no selective dependency.

The most robust biomarker [gene=PSAT1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.986]. Its protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort, but its cell of origin differs between single-cell datasets. It is not a subgroup marker and has no treatment association.

Robust tubule-loss biomarker whose protein loss and both phosphosites replicate [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819]. Its RNA ccA/ccB difference is not seen at protein level.

Strong loss of a tubule metabolic enzyme on frequently lost 14q, but its biomarker-profile position depends on the weights [gene=ALDH6A1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=33].

Exploratory: tumour-cell-derived transmembrane collagen [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881] that replicates in TCGA, survives the purity check and has antibody tractability. Main limitations: no selective dependency, heterogeneous expression across tumour cells, and untested normal-tissue protein staining.

Exploratory: tumour-cell Rab GTPase that holds at full purity [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189] and replicates in TCGA. Main limitation: it is an intracellular GTPase with a doubtful surface annotation and no dependency evidence.

Exploratory: secreted fibroblast gene [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647] that holds at full purity and has antibody tractability. Main limitation: it acts on the stroma rather than the tumour cell, has colon expression and has no dependency evidence.

limitations.text: Automatic checks establish evidence linkage and numeric bindings only. They do not validate causal interpretations, treatment efficacy or every sentence.

No candidate except EPAS1 shows a selective ccRCC cell-line dependency, and even that one is borderline after correction, so most target calls rest on expression selectivity and antibody, imaging or conjugate delivery.

Bulk tumour-versus-normal comparisons are confounded by loss of normal tubule tissue and by immune and stromal infiltration. Purity extrapolation and single-cell attribution reduce but do not remove this.
The single-cell and spatial datasets cover few donors, and endothelium and fibroblasts are small populations. SCARB1 and PSAT1 attributions differ between datasets.
CA9 and CD70 could not be tested in the confirmatory proteomic cohort because of too few matched pairs.
Treatment-response associations come from modest trial arms, and no gene differs between arms after correction.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses. Novelty is counted by gene-symbol literature searches, and none of them has functional, staining or dependency validation.
Structural-context scores describe cavities in predicted monomers. They are not evidence of a degron, of ligase compatibility or of degradability.
The literature corpus is a limited set of ccRCC abstracts with sentence-level extraction, so absence of a relation is not evidence of absence.

During verification, numbers in the agent findings were rewritten as canonical metric annotations, and literature numbers with no matching record field were rephrased in words; one HK2 confirmatory finding was added to the applied-agent input from the confirmatory record.
